rules.unit: One row per Atlas registry slug. A research record that covers several registry feeds (NJ Transit, MTA New York City Transit) appears on each of them.

definitionStatus.verified: A current official page publishes a named frequent tier; the quote was machine-checked against the saved page text.
definitionStatus.not-found-on-recheck: Earlier research recorded a definition, but the 2026-10-11 recheck found no named frequent tier on current official pages (often the earlier record was a list of route frequencies).
definitionStatus.narrow-scope: A machine-checked quote exists, but it covers one route, one line, part of the service area or a future target, not a network-wide frequent tier. Not a definition for comparison.
definitionStatus.planned-or-proposed: A machine-checked quote exists, but it comes from a plan describing a proposed or future network, or uses "frequent" as an analytical or land-use term. Not a tier in operation today.
definitionStatus.unnamed-frequency-bands: The current map publishes frequency classes (for example 15/30/60 minutes) without naming a frequent tier.
definitionStatus.image-only: The definition appears only in a map image; no machine-checkable quote.
definitionStatus.fetch-blocked: The official site blocks automated fetches; not rechecked.
definitionStatus.no-definition-found: Neither research set found a definition; not rechecked.

rules.thresholdMinutes: The slowest headway the source gives for the tier in its main weekday daytime period (for example "every 15-20 minutes on weekdays" is 20). Other periods stay in span. Null when no number is published.
rules.conflicts: When official sources disagree, the narrower definition is used and the row is marked conflictingSources.
